subject: gk
question: Which of the following causes the Tsunami waves?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Interior of the earth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Earthquakes occurring under the sea or ocean floor are the primary cause of tsunami waves.

• These seismic activities result in a sudden displacement of a large volume of water, generating waves that travel across the ocean at high speeds.

• Volcanic eruptions and underwater landslides can also contribute to the formation of tsunamis.

• The energy released by these geological activities within the earth’s interior can displace water vertically, creating waves that can travel long distances and cause significant damage upon reaching coastal areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Tsunami**

• A tsunami is a series of ocean waves with extremely long wavelengths caused by large-scale disturbances of the ocean, such as earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, or underwater landslides.

• When the ocean floor abruptly deforms and displaces the overlying water, it triggers a series of waves that can travel across entire ocean basins.

• Tsunamis are different from normal sea waves as their wavelengths are much longer, and they travel at much higher speeds.

• In deep water, tsunami waves may not be noticeable, but as they approach shallower coastal areas, they can increase in height dramatically and cause widespread destruction.

• **Earthquake**

• An earthquake is the shaking of the surface of the Earth resulting from a sudden release of energy in the Earth's lithosphere that creates seismic waves.

• Earthquakes can range in size from those that are so weak that they cannot be felt to those violent enough to toss people around and destroy whole cities.

• The seismicity, or seismic activity, of an area refers to the frequency, type, and size of earthquakes experienced over a period of time.

• **Volcanic Eruption**

• A volcanic eruption occurs when magma from beneath the Earth's crust is expelled through a volcano.

• Eruptions can release lava, ash, and gases that can cause widespread damage and affect global climates.

• Underwater volcanic eruptions can displace water and generate tsunamis.

• **Underwater Landslide**

• Underwater landslides, or submarine landslides, occur when sediments on the continental shelf or slope become destabilized and move downslope under the influence of gravity.

• These landslides can trigger tsunamis by displacing large volumes of water.
